    Here's the ecological function of each, backed by the observed records:
    
    Wrightia tinctoria (515 obs) — Primary coloniser. It's the first to establish on degraded, exposed soils. Its deep taproot breaks hardpan, improves infiltration, and creates shaded microsites for other species. It's your soil-prep species.
    
    Butea monosperma (489 obs) — Nitrogen-fixer + keystone resource. Legume family, fixes N into poor soil. Its bright flowers are a critical dry-season nectar source for sunbirds and parakeets (Feb–Mar). Seeds feed livestock and wildlife. The broad leaf litter suppresses weeds and builds humus.
    
    Albizia amara (175 obs) — Nitrogen-fixer + shade nurse. Another legume that inoculates poor soil. Spreading canopy shades the ground, reduces evaporation, and shelters slower-growing saplings. Excellent for interplanting.
    
    Ziziphus mauritiana (217 obs) — Wildlife fruit + thorn barrier. Berries feed birds, foxes, and monkeys through winter (Dec–Feb fruiting). Thorny thicket structure deters grazing animals from entering restoration plots — acts as a natural protector fence.
    
    Anogeissus latifolia (113 obs) — Climax canopy builder. The dominant dry-deciduous species. Deep roots, dense crown, massive leaf litter for soil carbon. Fruiting Oct–Dec (perfect: collect seed → plant at monsoon onset). Slow start but the long-term backbone.
    
    Two more I'd add for dry scrub:
    - Chloroxylon swietenia (147 obs, Satinwood) — canopy tree, pollinator value, commercial incentive to protect
    - Hardwickia binata (63 obs, Anjan) — legume N-fixer, excellent fodder, drought-hardy
    
    Seed-collection timing (from phenology data, 9–79 annotated records per species):
    - Sep–Oct: Albizia amara, Wrightia tinctoria, Anogeissus latifolia ← collect now-ish
    - Mar–Apr: Butea monosperma
    - Dec–Feb: Ziziphus mauritiana
    
    In short: Wrightia + Butea + Albizia = the soil-building pioneer team (N-fix + hardpan break + canopy). Ziziphus = wildlife attractor + living fence. Anogeissus = the climax goal. They complement each other — no single species does all.
